enabled_upstream_skills.name: get_state
enabled_upstream_skills.description: Read proprioception: joint positions (rad), fingertip grasp-point positions (m, world frame), gripper apertures (0 closed .. 1 open) and the calibrated gripper width rule (opening_width_m, grasp_state held_by_width | ambiguous | empty with the thresholds held_width_min_m / empty_close_max_m) for both arms.

enabled_upstream_skills.name: set_gripper
enabled_upstream_skills.description: Command one gripper to a physical opening (`opening_width_m`, distance between finger pads, 0..0.096 m) or a normalised `aperture` (0 closed .. 1 open), then wait `duration` seconds. Returns the calibrated measured opening and its width rule: grasp_state held_by_width (opening >= held_width_min_m: something is between the pads), empty (<= empty_close_max_m: closed on nothing) or ambiguous, from this gripper's calibration. When closing, `blocked=true` means the fingers stopped clearly before the commanded width - evidence, not proof, of a grasp.
enabled_upstream_skills.adaptation_note: Typed Hexfellow recipe with policy-supplied base-frame geometry; not the original physapi implementation. See adaptation guide.

enabled_upstream_skills.name: wait
enabled_upstream_skills.description: Hold the current command for `seconds` (lets objects settle).
enabled_upstream_skills.adaptation_note: Typed Hexfellow recipe with policy-supplied base-frame geometry; not the original physapi implementation. See adaptation guide.

enabled_upstream_skills.name: capture_image
enabled_upstream_skills.description: Capture an RGB image from a camera (top, left_wrist, right_wrist). The image is returned to the caller as an observation.

enabled_upstream_skills.name: run_sequence
enabled_upstream_skills.description: Execute a short plan: a list of skill calls [{skill, params}, ...] run in order, stopping at the first call whose status is not success (or at the first error). Use it to commit a multi-step plan in one turn (e.g. pick then place then reset_arms). Each step is executed and recorded exactly like a direct call and counts against the same budgets; nothing is skipped or simulated.
enabled_upstream_skills.adaptation_note: Typed Hexfellow recipe with policy-supplied base-frame geometry; not the original physapi implementation. See adaptation guide.

enabled_upstream_skills.name: ask_runtime_model
enabled_upstream_skills.description: Ask the runtime vision-language model a question about the current scene using the latest deployable observations (top RGB + colourised depth, wrist RGBs, gripper readings). Use for checks the geometric tools cannot answer (e.g. 'is the red block inside the red container?'). Answers are model judgements, not ground truth.

enabled_upstream_skills.name: verify_grasp
enabled_upstream_skills.description: Model-backed grasp verification for one gripper: the calibrated reading (opening width, blocked, width rule held_by_width / ambiguous / empty), wrist view, top RGB + depth and optional before-frames decide status held / not_held / uncertain and whether the held object is the target. Model verdict x width rule (outputs.decision): held needs both; model held on an empty-close width -> not_held; model not_held against a held-by-width opening -> not_held + width_conflict (the test lift decides); model unavailable -> uncertain + proprio_fallback held_proprio_only. Not proof. Call after closing, after a small lift, before transport, on suspected slip.

enabled_upstream_skills.name: solve_ik
enabled_upstream_skills.description: Check whether a fingertip target with a top-down wrist (optional yaw) - or a wrist pitched `pitch_deg` about the closing axis (as move_to / pick_tall_object use) - is reachable for one arm, with the joint-limit margin and manipulability of the solution (low margin = reach edge = poor accuracy). `full_column=true` also checks that the heights `column_heights` above the target (default 0, +3, +10 cm: grasp, test lift, approach/lift) are reachable on ONE wrist branch and reports the reach ceiling above the point. Does not move the robot.

enabled_upstream_skills.name: move_to
enabled_upstream_skills.description: Move one arm so its fingertip grasp point reaches a world position, wrist top-down (no collision avoidance; reach ceiling ~z 0.90 m) or pitched by `pitch_deg` about the closing axis (60 deg reaches z ~1.05 m). Duration scales with distance unless given; `cartesian=true` = straight line. FK measures the error after the move; `correction_passes` re-solve the residual (> 1 cm left at low margin = reach edge: pull_toward_base).
enabled_upstream_skills.adaptation_note: Typed Hexfellow recipe with policy-supplied base-frame geometry; not the original physapi implementation. See adaptation guide.

enabled_upstream_skills.name: pull_toward_base
enabled_upstream_skills.description: Rake an object at the reach edge toward the arm base: gripper open, fingertip on the base side of the object at contact height so the FAR finger pad (4.75 cm beyond the tip) sits behind it, then dragged `distance` (shortened to what is reachable) toward the base or `direction_xy`, then lifted. The drag is PLANNED before any motion: an infeasible drag fails at once with 0 s (metrics.preflight) - then pick with a LOW column (approach_height 0.04, lift_height 0.05) if solve_ik allows, or use the other arm / transfer. Object <= 7 cm tall, <= 8 cm along the pull; re-localise afterwards.
enabled_upstream_skills.adaptation_note: Typed Hexfellow recipe with policy-supplied base-frame geometry; not the original physapi implementation. See adaptation guide.

enabled_upstream_skills.name: reset_arms
enabled_upstream_skills.description: Move both arms back to the home configuration (grippers open). `duration` is a minimum: it is raised to the shortest time the joint rate clamp allows for the largest joint displacement (~1.05 s per rad), and the arms settle (<= 0.3 s) before the home joint error is measured - a short duration from a far pose is executed at the rate floor instead of failing.

Top-down pick; refused while the arm already holds something. Evidence: calibrated opening, 3 cm test lift, lift, verify_grasp (not_held against an object-sized opening: the test lift decides). `exclusive_of` (the container it stands in): only-the-target check, held-but-not-target = wrong_object (released). Empty pads -> one re-grasp at a fresh estimate. Pads never below the table or `pad_floor_z` (a rim; measured: pad_gate).
enabled_upstream_skills.name: pick
enabled_upstream_skills.adaptation_note: Typed Hexfellow recipe with policy-supplied base-frame geometry; not the original physapi implementation. See adaptation guide.

enabled_upstream_skills.name: place
enabled_upstream_skills.adaptation_note: Typed Hexfellow recipe with policy-supplied base-frame geometry; not the original physapi implementation. See adaptation guide.

enabled_upstream_skills.description: Pick at pick_xyz and place at place_xyz. side='auto' takes the arm whose approach and release columns are both reachable (larger joint-limit margin wins); when no single arm reaches both - or the given arm cannot reach the release column - and allow_transfer is true, the object is picked by the arm that reaches it, handed over with transfer_between_arms and placed by the other arm: one call for a cross-side relay. The route is decided by IK before any motion (a route-less call moves nothing).
enabled_upstream_skills.name: pick_and_place
enabled_upstream_skills.adaptation_note: Typed Hexfellow recipe with policy-supplied base-frame geometry; not the original physapi implementation. See adaptation guide.

enabled_upstream_skills.name: move_above
enabled_upstream_skills.description: Move an arm's fingertip to a point `height` above a world xy location (safe transit / inspection pose). Duration scales with the distance. A height above the reach ceiling at that xy is clamped to the highest reachable one (>= 3 cm) instead of failing (metrics.clamped, height_used).
enabled_upstream_skills.adaptation_note: Typed Hexfellow recipe with policy-supplied base-frame geometry; not the original physapi implementation. See adaptation guide.

enabled_upstream_skills.name: move_both
enabled_upstream_skills.description: Move BOTH fingertip grasp points to two world targets (>= 12 cm apart) in one synchronised motion. With `cartesian=true` (default) both tips follow straight lines, so the tip-to-tip distance is held by construction (drift < 1 cm); a path leaving the top-down reach (e.g. from home) falls back to joint space plus a short Cartesian finish (metrics.path). `keep_relation` aborts on tip-to-tip distance / height drift (co-held object). No collision avoidance.
enabled_upstream_skills.adaptation_note: Typed Hexfellow recipe with policy-supplied base-frame geometry; not the original physapi implementation. See adaptation guide.

enabled_upstream_skills.name: pinch_cloth
enabled_upstream_skills.description: Pinch flat cloth (towel corner / edge) at a table-plane point with one arm: open, approach, descend so the finger pads touch the table at the point (the tip height comes from the table - do NOT aim the tip at the cloth), close, verify the opening after closing and after a 2 cm test lift (one layer ~1 cm; empty = the calibrated empty-close width; > 2.5 cm = bunched layers that slip; a drop of more than half at the test lift = slipping). A failed first pinch is retried `slide_m` further onto the cloth along `slide_direction_xy`. Ends holding the pinch 2 cm up.
enabled_upstream_skills.adaptation_note: Typed Hexfellow recipe with policy-supplied base-frame geometry; not the original physapi implementation. See adaptation guide.

enabled_upstream_skills.name: bimanual_lift
enabled_upstream_skills.description: Grasp ONE object at two points (left arm at `left_xyz`, right arm at `right_xyz`), verify both grasps, then lift both synchronously by AT LEAST `lift_height` keeping the object level. Wrist branches keep the wrist cameras clear of each other (same grasp; a camera may then face away from the object). The lift is MEASURED: targets = tips measured after closing + lift_height + 1.5 cm (up to the reach ceiling), the per-side rise is read back by FK, a shortfall is re-commanded once and the achieved rise is reported (metrics.rise_m). Verified by calibrated openings after closing and a 2 cm test lift.
enabled_upstream_skills.adaptation_note: Typed Hexfellow recipe with policy-supplied base-frame geometry; not the original physapi implementation. See adaptation guide.

enabled_upstream_skills.name: fold_cloth
enabled_upstream_skills.description: Folds a flat cloth edge onto the opposite edge with both arms from its four footprint corners (segment_objects corners_xy), then MEASURES both moved corners (top depth camera, +-5 mm) against `corner_tolerance_m`; `nudge` = align_corner on off-tolerance corners. Lost pinch, short release, corners off or unmeasurable = PARTIAL (next_actions).
enabled_upstream_skills.adaptation_note: Typed Hexfellow recipe with policy-supplied base-frame geometry; not the original physapi implementation. See adaptation guide.

enabled_upstream_skills.name: repair_corner
enabled_upstream_skills.description: Move ONE cloth corner onto its target with one arm - the repair after a PARTIAL fold_cloth (use its outputs.next_action as is): the corner at `corner_xy` is pinched 12 mm inside / 20 mm along the edge, pads just above the fixed layer (`on_layer`, 12 mm) or the table, one layer only (opening from the calibrated held threshold up to 16 mm; a crumpled corner is released untouched), on ONE continuous path (lift 3, carry 6, release 4 cm up) to 1 cm short of `target_xy`. Re-observe once afterwards.
enabled_upstream_skills.adaptation_note: Typed Hexfellow recipe with policy-supplied base-frame geometry; not the original physapi implementation. See adaptation guide.

enabled_upstream_skills.name: bimanual_fold
enabled_upstream_skills.description: Two-point cloth fold, the 1.2.0 contract on the fold_cloth 1.1 mechanics: the left arm pinches the corner at `left_xyz`, the right at `right_xyz` (x, y only; pads 3 mm above the table, 12 mm inside the corner, 20 mm along the edge, ramped close, one re-pinch per side) and both are carried on ONE continuous path (carry 8 cm, release 5 cm up) onto `left_target_xy` / `right_target_xy`. Prefer fold_cloth (four footprint corners).
enabled_upstream_skills.adaptation_note: Typed Hexfellow recipe with policy-supplied base-frame geometry; not the original physapi implementation. See adaptation guide.

enabled_upstream_skills.name: hold_and_push
enabled_upstream_skills.description: Fixture-and-operate: `hold_side` presses closed fingertips onto `hold_xyz` (holding a container / base in place) while `push_side` pushes from behind `start_xyz` toward `goal_xy` at `contact_height` (fingertip height above the table) in four Cartesian segments. The holder's fingertip drift is checked between segments; more than `hold_tolerance_m` aborts the push. Durations scale with distance.
enabled_upstream_skills.adaptation_note: Typed Hexfellow recipe with policy-supplied base-frame geometry; not the original physapi implementation. See adaptation guide.

enabled_upstream_skills.name: transfer_between_arms
enabled_upstream_skills.description: Move a held object from one arm to the other via the table: picks a shared staging point both arms reach top-down with joint-limit margin (or `staging_xy`), clamps transit / release / approach heights to each arm's reach ceiling, places the object with the giver, retreats the giver to its own side, and regrasps with the receiver's verified pick (optionally re-localised by `relocate_color`).
enabled_upstream_skills.adaptation_note: Typed Hexfellow recipe with policy-supplied base-frame geometry; not the original physapi implementation. See adaptation guide.

enabled_upstream_skills.name: pixel_to_world
enabled_upstream_skills.description: Top-camera pixels -> world positions: a single (u, v) or a BATCH points=[[u, v], ...] (<= 16) in ONE call (one query unit). Without height_m the depth image gives the surface point (source 'depth'); with height_m the ray meets z = table + height_m (source 'plane_given_height'); no valid depth -> table plane, flagged (source 'plane_table_fallback_no_depth'). Prefer segment_objects / locate_objects geometry (corners, faces) over probing edges pixel by pixel.

enabled_upstream_skills.name: extract_from_container
enabled_upstream_skills.description: Take an object protruding >= 3 cm from a container out (refused while the arm holds something): verified `pick` `grasp_below_top_m` below the object top (pads kept above the rim by a measured gate), lift to the reach ceiling, DECISIVE target-only check (top depth rim ring, SAM3 `container_prompt`; a container-sized or mixed grasp is released back and re-grasped ONCE higher), then move `clearance_m` sideways once the object bottom clears the rim. Heights = table z + estimated_height_m.
enabled_upstream_skills.adaptation_note: Typed Hexfellow recipe with policy-supplied base-frame geometry; not the original physapi implementation. See adaptation guide.

enabled_upstream_skills.name: insert_into_container
enabled_upstream_skills.description: Put the object the arm ALREADY HOLDS INTO a container - also the call to re-align a held object: carry over the opening, re-centre on the rim ring (top depth), descend in 1 cm steps to contact or `max_descent_m` (pads above the rim), guided release, retreat, confirm (depth); a stall at rim height is retried on `search_offsets` offsets. A reach-edge carry pose fails BEFORE moving, object still held: never call pick / extract_from_container then (they open the gripper) - transfer_between_arms, or place and re-pick lower.
enabled_upstream_skills.adaptation_note: Typed Hexfellow recipe with policy-supplied base-frame geometry; not the original physapi implementation. See adaptation guide.

enabled_upstream_skills.name: sweep_area
enabled_upstream_skills.description: Wipe an axis-aligned table patch with the closed fingers: parallel Cartesian strokes along `direction_xy` keeping the finger tips `contact_height` above the table (no bowing). The low part of the closed fingers is a ~1.2 cm column, so each stroke clears ~1.2 cm + the debris size; passes are spaced by that band up to `max_passes` (a 15 cm patch needs ~8 passes, ~45 s). Strokes start `run_in` before the patch and end `overshoot` beyond it. Default direction: along y away from the table centre-line.
enabled_upstream_skills.adaptation_note: Typed Hexfellow recipe with policy-supplied base-frame geometry; not the original physapi implementation. See adaptation guide.

enabled_upstream_skills.name: push_until_stop
enabled_upstream_skills.description: Push with the closed fingers along `direction_xy` against the object face at `contact_xyz` (fingertip height; pads kept >= 2 mm above the table; calibrated pad offset and 1-3 cm finger-link lead on tall faces accounted for) in `step_m` Cartesian steps at constant height until the tip stalls (end-stop, obstacle), the reach limit, or `max_travel`. A stall with travel >= `min_travel` is SUCCESS: what closing a drawer looks like.
enabled_upstream_skills.adaptation_note: Typed Hexfellow recipe with policy-supplied base-frame geometry; not the original physapi implementation. See adaptation guide.

enabled_upstream_skills.name: push
enabled_upstream_skills.description: Push an object on the table: closed fingertips placed `standoff` behind the object (opposite the push direction), then a Cartesian stroke at constant height to the goal. `contact_height` is the height of the closed-finger PAD BOTTOMS above the table (the fingertip point sits the calibrated pad offset higher: 0.017 m in sim). The stroke stops when the fingertip stalls; a stall after at least half of the requested distance counts as success with metrics.stalled=true (end-stop reached). For drawers/lids prefer `push_until_stop`.
enabled_upstream_skills.adaptation_note: Typed Hexfellow recipe with policy-supplied base-frame geometry; not the original physapi implementation. See adaptation guide.

enabled_upstream_skills.name: align_corner
enabled_upstream_skills.description: Nudge ONE landed cloth corner by a measured offset with one arm (fold_cloth's finishing move; a remaining call is in its outputs.next_actions): pinch the top-layer flap just inside `corner_xy` (ONE layer only - wider = crumpled, released untouched), lift, carry so the corner stops `stop_short_m` before `target_xy` (offsets 3-80 mm), lower, open IN PLACE. Offsets > 6 cm: repair_corner. Re-measure afterwards.
enabled_upstream_skills.adaptation_note: Typed Hexfellow recipe with policy-supplied base-frame geometry; not the original physapi implementation. See adaptation guide.

enabled_upstream_skills.name: pick_tall_object
enabled_upstream_skills.description: Pick a TALL standing object (bottle, can) with a PITCHED wrist: approach tilted pitch_deg from vertical toward +x, fingers closing across the object grasp_height_m above the table (default 60 % of its height); reaches where a top-down wrist cannot. Top and footprint centre are re-measured from the top depth camera first. Swings in above all object tops, then down and forward from the robots' side: give the other objects as obstacles_xy, nearest object first. Lying objects (top < 10 cm): use pick.
enabled_upstream_skills.adaptation_note: Typed Hexfellow recipe with policy-supplied base-frame geometry; not the original physapi implementation. See adaptation guide.

enabled_upstream_skills.name: place_into_bin
enabled_upstream_skills.description: Drop the held object INTO an open container (bin; rim above the top-down reach), wrist pitched. The rim ring is found in the top depth image within 25 cm of container_xyz (an off centre is corrected; no ring = refused). Lifts straight up (verified), carries over a free spot inside the opening, lowers until the pads are just above the rim, releases. Never releases on or above the rim (object kept).
enabled_upstream_skills.adaptation_note: Typed Hexfellow recipe with policy-supplied base-frame geometry; not the original physapi implementation. See adaptation guide.

enabled_upstream_skills.name: pick_and_place_tall_object
enabled_upstream_skills.description: Bin one tall object (bottle, can): standing (top >= 10 cm) -> pick_tall_object (pitched wrist); LYING (top < 10 cm, depth-checked) -> top-down pick across its axis; then place_into_bin (carry over the rim, free spot inside; geometry from depth). side='auto' = arm by reach. Neighbours: obstacles_xy; nearest first.
enabled_upstream_skills.adaptation_note: Typed Hexfellow recipe with policy-supplied base-frame geometry; not the original physapi implementation. See adaptation guide.

enabled_upstream_skills.name: pick_rim
enabled_upstream_skills.description: Grasp a wide / flared round object (bowl, plate) by its RIM: grasp point on the rim nearest the arm base (or along `grasp_direction_xy`), radial pinch across the wall, pads 2 cm below the rim. Use instead of pick for anything wider than ~8 cm (a body grasp hooks the flared rim on release). A rim-held bowl hangs tilted ~20 deg (far side down): on a NARROW support (rack) grasp along its long axis. Runs the verified pick; after a miss the rim point is re-planned once from a fresh detection.
enabled_upstream_skills.adaptation_note: Typed Hexfellow recipe with policy-supplied base-frame geometry; not the original physapi implementation. See adaptation guide.

enabled_upstream_skills.name: set_down
enabled_upstream_skills.description: Set the held object down onto a support (table, rack, tray) with its centre at `object_xy`: carry over the point (bottom 3 cm above), descend to touchdown (stall) or `support_z`, release, retreat, confirm from depth that it rests there (metrics.settled, landing_offset_m). Offsets from pick_rim: centre_offset_xy (tip -> object centre), object_bottom_offset_m (tip above the bottom); centred pick: [0, 0], grasp height. A raised support's TOP (rails above a base plate) is re-measured from depth (metrics.support_measured); on a RAISED narrow support a rim-held object is turned so its tilt lies along the rails (metrics.alignment).
enabled_upstream_skills.adaptation_note: Typed Hexfellow recipe with policy-supplied base-frame geometry; not the original physapi implementation. See adaptation guide.

enabled_upstream_skills.name: insert_onto_peg
enabled_upstream_skills.description: Lower a held object with a hole (nut, ring) onto a peg until it rests: peg re-localised from depth, hover 1.5 cm above the peg, re-centre the hole on it (depth), descend past the peg top in 1 cm steps (retries on measured / blind offsets), seat it, CHECK the seat before letting go (a jammed nut is lifted back, not released), release, verify. hole_xy_at_grasp = hole centre when grasped (segment_objects: the ring part's centre); grasp_xy / grasp_z / yaw = the pick's grasp (else pass the pick's yaw as grasp_yaw).
enabled_upstream_skills.adaptation_note: Typed Hexfellow recipe with policy-supplied base-frame geometry; not the original physapi implementation. See adaptation guide.
